# Clean Architecture - Quick Visual Reference

**One-page guide to understanding the 4-layer separation**

---

## ?? The 4 Layers at a Glance

```
???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
? ?? API LAYER                                                ?
?    (HTTP, gRPC, Consumers)                                  ?
?    ? Controllers                                            ?
?    ? Middleware                                             ?
?    ? Message Consumers                                      ?
?    ? Program.cs (DI setup)                                  ?
?    References: Application layer                            ?
???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
                         ? depends on
???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
? ?? APPLICATION LAYER                                        ?
?    (Orchestration, Use Cases)                               ?
?    ? Command Handlers                                       ?
?    ? Query Handlers                                         ?
?    ? Service Interfaces (abstractions)                      ?
?    ? DTOs                                                   ?
?    References: Domain, uses abstractions                    ?
???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
                         ? depends on
???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
? ??? DOMAIN LAYER                                            ?
?    (Business Logic, Entities)                               ?
?    ? Entities (Order, OrderItem)                            ?
?    ? Enums (OrderStatus)                                    ?
?    ? Repository Interfaces (IOrderRepository)               ?
?    ? Business Rules & Validation                            ?

???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????

        ? implemented by ?

???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
? ?? INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER                                     ?
?    (Implementation Details)                                 ?
?    ? DbContext (EF Core)                                    ?
?    ? Repository Implementations                             ?
?    ? Event Publisher Implementations                        ?
?    ? Message Consumers                                      ?

???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
```

## ?? Request Flow Through Layers

### "Pay for an order" request

```
HTTP POST /api/orders/{id}/pay
    ?
?? API LAYER ?????????????????????????????????
? OrdersCommandController.Pay(orderId)       ?
? ?? Converts HTTP ? PayOrderCommand         ?
? ?? Sends to MediatR                        ?
????????????????????????????????????????????
             ?
?? APPLICATION LAYER ?????????????????????????
? PayOrderCommandHandler.Handle()            ?
? ?? Calls IOrderRepository (abstraction)    ?
? ?? Calls Order.MarkAsPaid() (domain)       ?
? ?? Calls IEventPublisher (abstraction)     ?
????????????????????????????????????????????
             ?
?? DOMAIN LAYER ??????????????????????????????
? Order.MarkAsPaid()                         ?
? ?? Validates: Status is Pending?           ?
? ?? Changes Status ? Paid                   ?
???????????????????????????????????????????????
             ?
?? INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER ??????????????????????
? 1. OrderRepository.GetByIdAsync()          ?
?    ?? Uses OrdersDbContext ? SQL Server    ?
?                                            ?
? 2. MassTransitEventPublisher.PublishAsync()?
?    ?? Creates OutboxMessage                ?
?    ?? Saves to database                    ?
???????????????????????????????????????????????
```

## ?? Each Layer's Responsibility

### DOMAIN Layer

```csharp
// ? Pure Business Logic
public class Order
{
    public void MarkAsPaid()
    {
        if (Status == OrderStatus.Paid) return;
        if (Status != OrderStatus.Pending) return;
        Status = OrderStatus.Paid;
    }
}

// ? Only C# classes
// ? No database
// ? No HTTP
// ? No external services
```

**Responsibility:** "What are the rules?"

---

### APPLICATION Layer

```csharp
// ? Orchestration
public class PayOrderCommandHandler : IRequestHandler<PayOrderCommand>
{
    private readonly IOrderRepository _repo;
    private readonly IEventPublisher _publisher;

    public async Task Handle(PayOrderCommand req, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var order = await _repo.GetByIdAsync(req.OrderId, ct);

        if (order?.Status != OrderStatus.Pending)
            throw new Exception("Not payable");

        await _publisher.PublishAsync(
            new OrderPaymentRequested(order.Id, order.CustomerId, order.TotalPrice)
        );
    }
}

// ? Uses abstractions (IOrderRepository, IEventPublisher)
// ? Orchestrates domain logic
// ? No database code
// ? No HTTP code
```

**Responsibility:** "How should this work?"

---

### INFRASTRUCTURE Layer

```csharp
// ? Implementation Details
public class OrderRepository : IOrderRepository
{
    private readonly OrdersDbContext _dbContext;

    public async Task AddAsync(Order order, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        _dbContext.Orders.Add(order);
        await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
    }
}

public class MassTransitEventPublisher : IEventPublisher
{
    public async Task PublishAsync<T>(T message) where T : class
    {
        var outboxMessage = new OutboxMessage
        {
            Content = JsonSerializer.Serialize(message),
            Type = typeof(T).AssemblyQualifiedName
        };
        _dbContext.OutboxMessages.Add(outboxMessage);
        await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
    }
}

// ? EF Core code
// ? Database queries
// ? External service calls
// ? Implements interfaces from Application layer
```

**Responsibility:** "How do we actually do it?"

---

### API Layer

```csharp
// ? HTTP Handling
[ApiController]
[Route("api/orders/commands")]
public class OrdersCommandController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly IMediator _mediator;

    [HttpPost("{orderId:guid}/pay")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Pay(Guid orderId)
    {
        await _mediator.Send(new PayOrderCommand(orderId));
        return NoContent();
    }
}

// ? HTTP endpoints
// ? Controllers
// ? Message consumers
// ? Delegates to Application layer
```

**Responsibility:** "How do requests come in?"

---

## ?? Why Each Layer Exists

### Domain Layer
```
WHY: Business logic must be independent of technology

BENEFIT:
? Testable without infrastructure
? Reusable in any context
? Technology decisions don't affect it
? Represents intellectual property of business
```

### Application Layer
```
WHY: Orchestration must be independent of how it's done

BENEFIT:
? Can swap implementations (SQL ? Mongo)
? Reuse same logic in multiple entry points
? Clear separation of concerns
? Easy to test with mocks
```

### Infrastructure Layer
```
WHY: Implementation details in one place

BENEFIT:
? Easy to change database
? Easy to swap message broker
? All "gritty" code in one place
? Easy to mock for testing
```

### API Layer
```
WHY: HTTP handling separate from business logic

BENEFIT:
? Same logic works for gRPC, background jobs, etc.
? Easy to change API framework
? Clear request entry point
? Centralized DI setup
```

---

## ? Key Principles

### 1?? Dependency Rule
```
? Outer layers can depend on inner layers
? Inner layers NEVER depend on outer layers

   API ? Application ? Domain
   ? API can use Application ?
   ? Domain cannot use API ?
```

### 2?? Interface Segregation
```
Inner layers define interfaces
Outer layers implement interfaces

Domain defines: IOrderRepository
Infrastructure implements: OrderRepository
Application uses: IOrderRepository (abstraction)
```

### 3?? Single Responsibility
```
Domain:         "What is valid?"
Application:    "What to do and when?"
Infrastructure: "How to do it?"
API:            "Where requests come from?"
```

---

## ?? Swapping Implementations Example

### Scenario: Switch from SQL Server to MongoDB

**BEFORE:**
```
Application layer knows about:
- OrdersDbContext (EF Core)
- SQL Server queries
- SQL-specific operations

Result: Can't switch! Business logic is tightly coupled!
```

**AFTER (With Clean Architecture):**
```
Application layer knows about:
- IOrderRepository (abstraction)
- Business logic only

Infrastructure layer:
- Old: OrderRepository ? SQL Server
- New: MongoOrderRepository ? MongoDB

Same abstraction!
Just swap the registration:

// Old
builder.Services.AddScoped<IOrderRepository, OrderRepository>();

// New  
builder.Services.AddScoped<IOrderRepository, MongoOrderRepository>();

Everything else unchanged! ?
```

---

## ?? Layer Characteristics

| Aspect | Domain | Application | Infrastructure | API |
|--------|--------|-------------|-----------------|-----|
| **Has DB Code?** | ? | ? | ? | ? |
| **Has HTTP Code?** | ? | ? | ? | ? |
| **Has Business Rules?** | ? | Coordinates | ? | ? |
| **Has Abstractions?** | Defines | Uses | Implements | Uses |
| **Testable without infra?** | ? | ? | ? | Somewhat |
| **Independent?** | ? | Somewhat | ? | ? |

---

## ? Quick Checklist

When code asks: "Which layer do I belong in?"

```
? Does it have business rules?
   ? DOMAIN layer

? Does it coordinate multiple steps?
   ? APPLICATION layer

? Does it talk to database/external service?
   ? INFRASTRUCTURE layer

? Does it handle HTTP requests?
   ? API layer
```

---

## ?? Remember

```
Domain:         "What SHOULD happen?"
Application:    "WHAT to do and WHEN?"
Infrastructure: "HOW to do it?"
API:            "WHERE things enter?"

Each layer answers ONE question!
```
